findings.reason: without naming `require_setting` and the `SettingsFlags(machine=…)` shape, the builder either dereferences a possibly-None `Setting` or invents a second setting-read path beside the owner's.
findings.text: §3's "the entry point calls `resolve_settings().ids_root` with `pulse_path` and nothing else" describes reading `.ids_root` directly, but `ResolvedSettings.ids_root` is a `Setting` whose `.value` may be `None`, and the owner already carries the refusal helper for it (`require_setting("ids_root", settings.ids_root, …)`, `imas_alambic/cli.py:87`); the same sentence says the call is made "with `machine=\"jt-60sa\"`", but `resolve_settings` takes a `SettingsFlags`, and `ids_root` does not depend on the machine setting at all, so the stated reason ("ambix's bundle serves diii-d and mast as well") does not apply to the resolution §3 needs

findings.reason: the section fixes `_read_pulse_ids`'s location and shape, so leaving it script-local while calling it shared locks in the duplication instead of retiring it.
findings.text: §3 keeps `_read_pulse_ids` inside `scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py` and justifies it by saying jt60sa-pulse-ids §4 "shares it as the written-pulse reader", but a script is not an importable owner, so §4 must either import from a script path or re-implement the read — the third copy of the run-file layout that the pulse-ids review (`docs/plans/jt60sa-pulse-ids.html`: "the writer's output layout known in two places … with §4 about to add a third") set out to avoid; the owner to extend is the module that already owns the run-file name, `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/pulse_writer.py` (`pulse_path`, line 292), which should carry the paired reader
